extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent applicants, patent practitioners, and USPTO examiners handling petitions to revive or withdraw holdings of abandonment
extracted.subtask_short: petitions to revive abandoned patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for filing petitions to withdraw a holding of abandonment and petitions to revive unintentionally or unavoidably abandoned U.S. patent applications (37 CFR 1.137, 1.181, 1.8, related MPEP guidance), including required evidence, timeliness rules, reply content, fees, and special rules by application type and filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of timely filing — Express Mail/PALM entry
rubrics_metrics.description: When Express Mail is relied on to show timely filing, the paper must be entered in PALM with the 'Express Mail' date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Express Mail is claimed, the Office will use the Express Mail date entered in PALM as the filing/receipt date for the reply. Ensure the PALM entry reflects the Express Mail date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of timely filing — Postcard receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: A postcard receipt that properly identifies the reply provides prima facie evidence that the reply was timely filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reply was timely filed based on a postcard receipt, the reply must be entered into PALM using the date of receipt shown on the postcard. Example: if abandonment held for failure to reply to a first Office action and applicant has postcard receipt showing an amendment was timely filed, the holding of abandonment should be withdrawn upon filing a petition to withdraw.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of timely mailing — Certificate of Mailing under 37 CFR 1.8
rubrics_metrics.description: When relying on a certificate of mailing under 37 CFR 1.8 (but not a postcard receipt), the statement attesting to previous timely mailing must be on a personal knowledge basis or to the satisfaction of the Director of the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the attesting statement is not made by the person who signed the Certificate of Mailing (no personal knowledge), the statement should include supporting evidence (e.g., copies of a mailing log) showing correspondence was mailed. When timely filing is shown based on a certificate of mailing, the correspondence is entered into PALM with the actual date of receipt (date duplicate copy filed with the 1.8 statement). 37 CFR 1.8(b)(3) and MPEP § 512 provide details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and duplicate filing under 37 CFR 1.8(b)(3)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.8(b) permits applicant to notify the Office of a previous mailing and submit a statement under 1.8(b)(3) accompanied by a duplicate copy of the correspondence when a reasonable amount of time (e.g., more than one month) has elapsed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant need not wait until abandonment to notify the Office. Applicant should check private PAIR for status before notifying the Office. The duplicate copy and statement procedures affect PALM entry and proof of timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of petitions to withdraw holding of abandonment (37 CFR 1.181(f) — 2-month rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any petition under 37 CFR 1.181 not filed within 2 months from the action complained of may be dismissed as untimely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition to withdraw a holding of abandonment not filed within two months of the mail date of the notice of abandonment may be dismissed as untimely under 37 CFR 1.181(f). The Office may alternatively require a terminal disclaimer as a condition of granting an untimely petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer condition for certain pre-1995 applications (applicant received notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: In any design application, any utility application filed before June 8, 1995, and any plant application filed before June 8, 1995, if applicant receives a notice of abandonment, any petition to withdraw the holding of abandonment not filed within two months of the mail date of the notice will not (absent extraordinary circumstances) be treated on its merits unless accompanied by a terminal disclaimer under 37 CFR 1.321(a) and required fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The period to be disclaimed is the terminal part of the term of any patent granted on the application (or on any utility/plant application claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120/121/365(c)) equivalent to the period between (A) the date two months after the mail date of the notice of abandonment and (B) the filing date of a grantable petition to withdraw the holding of abandonment. Use PTO/SB/62 for terminal disclaimer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer condition for certain pre-1995 applications (applicant never received notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the same categories (design; utility/plant filed before June 8, 1995) if applicant never receives the notice of abandonment, any petition to withdraw not filed within twelve months from the date of applicant’s filing (or date of submission, if correspondence never received by the Office) for which further Office action could reasonably be expected will not (absent extraordinary circumstances) be treated on its merits unless accompanied by a terminal disclaimer under 37 CFR 1.321(a) and required fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The disclaimed period is the terminal part of the patent term equivalent to the period between (A) the date that is twelve months from applicant’s filing/submission for which further action could reasonably be expected and (B) the filing date of a grantable petition to withdraw the holding of abandonment. Use PTO/SB/62.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of untimely petitions by filing date ranges (June 8, 1995 to May 29, 2000)
rubrics_metrics.description: In utility and plant applications filed on or after June 8, 1995 but before May 29, 2000, a terminal disclaimer should not be required as a condition of granting an untimely petition to withdraw the holding of abandonment; consult OPLA if the abandonment involves appellate review, interference, or secrecy order suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPLA consultation is necessary if the holding of abandonment involves: (A) appellate review by the Board, (B) an interference under 35 U.S.C. 135(a), or (C) periods when application was sealed or prosecution suspended under secrecy order (35 U.S.C. 181) because patent term extension adjustments may need effecting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of untimely petitions by filing date ranges (on or after May 29, 2000)
rubrics_metrics.description: In utility and plant applications filed on or after May 29, 2000, a terminal disclaimer should not be required as a condition of granting an untimely petition to withdraw the holding of abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AIPA patent term adjustment provisions (37 CFR 1.704(c)(4) and 1.704(a)) automatically reduce PTA for petitions not filed within two months of a notice of abandonment; intentional delay may lead to dismissal under 37 CFR 1.181(f). Intentional delay also precludes relief under 37 CFR 1.137(a) or (b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for revival under 37 CFR 1.137
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.137 provides for revival of abandoned applications and lapsed patents for failure: (A) to timely reply to an Office requirement in a provisional application; (B) to timely prosecute in a nonprovisional application; (C) to timely pay the issue fee for a design application; (D) to timely pay the issue fee for a utility or plant application; and (E) to timely pay any outstanding balance of the issue fee (lapsed patents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each ground has specific reply requirements (see separate rubrics). Revival may be sought under either the 'unavoidable delay' standard (1.137(a), backed by evidence and possibly 35 U.S.C. 133 or 151) or the 'unintentional delay' standard (1.137(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for a petition under 37 CFR 1.137(a) (unavoidable delay)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.137(a) requires: (A) the required reply, unless previously filed; (B) the petition fee as set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(l); (C) a showing to the satisfaction of the Director that the entire delay was unavoidable; and (D) any terminal disclaimer required pursuant to 37 CFR 1.137(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition under 1.137(a) is more exacting and will typically require documentary evidence of procedures, training, docketing records, etc., to show the delay was unavoidable. The Director may require additional information where the unavoidability is in question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for a petition under 37 CFR 1.137(b) (unintentional delay)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.137(b) requires: (A) the required reply, unless previously filed; (B) the petition fee as set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(m); (C) a statement that the entire delay was unintentional; and (D) any terminal disclaimer required pursuant to 37 CFR 1.137(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions under (b) are less burdensome — the Office relies on statements of unintentional delay and the applicant's duty of candor. The Director may request further information in some cases, but most (b) petitions are granted on a practitioner's statement and minimal supporting correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply requirement — failure to pay issue or publication fee
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications abandoned for failure to pay the issue fee (or any portion thereof), the reply must include payment of the issue fee or outstanding balance. For abandonment for failure to pay a publication fee, the required reply must include payment of the publication fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a continuing application without payment of the issue or publication fee is not an acceptable reply in applications abandoned for failure to pay those fees. If an allowance notice required payment, any increase later may require payment of the balance as per In re Mills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply requirement — failure to reply to a non-final action
rubrics_metrics.description: In a nonprovisional application abandoned for failure to reply to a non-final action, the required reply may be either: (A) an argument or an amendment under 37 CFR 1.111; or (B) the filing of a continuing application under 37 CFR 1.53(b) (or a CPA under 1.53(d) for design applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition may be granted if the reply appears bona fide. After revival, the examiner may later determine the reply is deficient and give a 1-month shortened statutory period under 37 CFR 1.135(c) to correct; extensions under 1.136(a) are permitted. Failure to correct leads to abandonment again.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply requirement — failure to reply to a final action
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply under 37 CFR 1.113 to a final action must include a request for continued examination (RCE) under 37 CFR 1.114 or cancellation of, or appeal from, each rejected claim. Thus, for abandonment due to failure to reply to a final action, the required reply must be: (A) a Notice of Appeal and appeal fee; (B) an amendment under 37 CFR 1.116 that cancels all rejected claims or otherwise prima facie places the application in condition for allowance; (C) an RCE (with a submission meeting 1.111 and fee) for utility/plant filed on/after June 8, 1995; or (D) a continuing application under 1.53(b) (CPA under 1.53(d) for design).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a proposed amendment places the application in condition for allowance, the examiner should mark 'OK to enter upon revival.' If not, the examiner completes PTOL-303 and returns it to the Office of Petitions; the Office will not grant the petition in that case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply requirement — failure to file an appeal brief
rubrics_metrics.description: If abandonment occurred due to failure to file an appeal brief, the required reply must be either: (A) an appeal brief in compliance with 37 CFR 41.37(c) and fee; (B) an RCE with a submission and requisite fee (1.114) for utility/plant filed on/after June 8, 1995; or (C) a continuing application under 1.53(b) (or CPA under 1.53(d) for design).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a notice of appeal is used as the reply, the time period under 37 CFR 41.37 for filing the appeal brief will be set by the Director in the decision granting the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing an RCE as the required reply — responsiveness standard
rubrics_metrics.description: When an RCE is filed as the reply to revive an application abandoned for failure to reply to a final Office action or to file an appeal brief, the submission accompanying the RCE must be a reply responsive within the meaning of 37 CFR 1.111 to the last Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsiveness is judged without regard to the 'final' status of the action. The submission may be a previously filed amendment after final or a statement incorporating by reference prior arguments. The petition may be granted if the submission appears to be a bona fide attempt to provide a complete reply; later deficiencies may trigger a 1-month shortened period to correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office may require continuing application or RCE when reply would place inordinate burden on Office
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may require the filing of a continuing application or an RCE to meet the reply requirement of 37 CFR 1.137 where treating a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 or 1.113 would place an inordinate burden on the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemplary circumstances: (A) application abandoned for an inordinate period of time; (B) file contains multiple or conflicting replies to the last Office action; (C) the reply(s) submitted under 1.137 are questionable as to compliance with 1.111 or 1.113.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification requirement after nonpublication request and foreign filing (45-day rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant made a nonpublication request and then files a counterpart application in a foreign country (or under a multilateral agreement requiring 18-month publication), the applicant must notify the USPTO of the foreign filing within forty-five days after the date of such foreign filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely provide this notice results in abandonment under 35 U.S.C. 122(b)(2)(B)(iii). Revival of such abandonment is available only on the basis of unintentional delay under 37 CFR 1.137(b) (not unavoidable). The reply requirement of 1.137(c) is met by the notification, but a petition under 1.137(b) will not stay any running reply periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition fee requirement — timing and nonrefundable nature
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to revive for unintentionally abandoned application or delayed issue fee must be accompanied by the petition fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(m), unless filed under 35 U.S.C. 133 or 151 (unavoidable delay), in which case fee per 37 CFR 1.17(l) applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition fee is required on filing (not merely on grant). The Office will not refund petition fees regardless of whether the petition is dismissed or denied, and will not reach merits of any petition lacking the requisite fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unintentional delay standard — reliance on statements and duty of candor
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions under 37 CFR 1.137(b) are evaluated under the less stringent 'unintentional delay' standard and the Office accepts the applicant’s statement that 'the entire delay ... was unintentional' without requiring further information in the vast majority of petitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office relies on the duty of candor (37 CFR 10.18) and may request further information in limited cases. Inappropriate statements may have adverse enforcement consequences (e.g., inequitable conduct findings). Applicants are advised to include the explicit unintentional-delay statement to expedite treatment and may use forms PTO/SB/64, PTO/SB/64a, PTO/SB/64PCT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unavoidable delay standard — evidentiary showing required
rubrics_metrics.description: A showing of unavoidable delay for petitions under 37 CFR 1.137(a) requires evidence concerning: (1) procedures in place that should have avoided the error; (2) training and experience of persons responsible; and (3) copies of docketing records to show the error caused the delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because 1.137(a) requires proving the delay was unavoidable (a higher standard), such petitions often require multiple interlocutory decisions and requests for additional evidence; many petitions initially filed under (a) are instead granted under (b) upon substitution of the less exacting unintentional standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intentional delay is not unintentional — enumerated examples
rubrics_metrics.description: A delay resulting from a deliberately chosen course of action is not 'unintentional' (e.g., applicant deliberately permits abandonment because claims considered unpatentable; to defer fees; to defer prosecution costs; or lack of commercial value).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples listed: (A) applicant does not consider claims patentable over cited references; (B) applicant considers allowed/patentable claims insufficient breadth to justify expense; (C) applicant does not consider patent of sufficient value; (D) applicant does not consider patent worth maintaining; (E) applicant seeks to defer fees/prosecution expenses. A later change of mind does not render a prior deliberate abandonment 'unintentional.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner handling of proposed replies upon revival
rubrics_metrics.description: If a proposed reply (to a non-final action) appears bona fide, the petition may be granted; the examiner may later determine defects and issue a 1-month shortened statutory period under 37 CFR 1.135(c) for correction. For replies to final actions, if the amendment places the application in condition for allowance, examiner should mark 'OK to enter upon revival'; otherwise examiner completes PTOL-303 and returns it to the Office of Petitions and the petition will not be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTOL-303 serves as an advisory notice; the courtesy copy is sent with the decision on the petition. Examiners should not mail PTOL-303 to applicant. IFW processing references apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended petition content and form (PTO/SB/64 checklist)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PTO/SB/64 (Petition for Revival under 37 CFR 1.137(b)) lists that a grantable petition requires: (1) petition fee; (2) reply and/or issue fee; (3) terminal disclaimer with disclaimer fee (required for all utility/plant applications filed before June 8, 1995, and all design applications); and (4) statement that the entire delay was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTO/SB/64 provides fields for docket number, inventor, application number, filing date, title, and instructions for submission to Office of Petitions. Use the form to expedite processing; contact Petitions Information if assistance is needed.
